He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

Secondary_Symptoms: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands
Swelling and erythema of the left wrist
Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Doctor, I’ve had 3 days of worsening pain in my left wrist, and this morning it got worse with chills and feeling really run down. I also noticed painless, purple bumps/blisters on both wrists and hands. The left wrist is swollen and very tender, and it hurts even when I move it passively.”

I’m sorry you’re dealing with this—let’s narrow it down quickly.

**Question 1 (one thing):** Do you have any **fever measured** (e.g., ≥38°C / 100.4°F) or is it mainly chills/feeling run down?
“Doctor, I haven’t taken my temperature, but I’ve had chills and I feel run down—no measured fever.”
**Question 2:** Are the purple bumps/blisters **raised and painful**, or are they truly **painless** (no tenderness when you touch them)?
“Doctor, they’re truly painless—I don’t feel tenderness when I touch those purple bumps/blisters on my wrists and hands.”
**Question 3:** Any **skin changes elsewhere**—for example, **mouth sores**, **eye redness/pain**, or **genital sores**?
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any mouth sores or eye redness/pain, and I haven’t had any genital sores either.”
**Question 4:** Do you have any **new medications** in the last 1–3 weeks (especially antibiotics, anti-seizure meds, allopurinol), or any recent **infection**?
“Doctor, no new medications in the last few weeks, and I don’t recall any specific illness besides the knee pain that resolved on its own—just the chills and wrist symptoms starting 3 days ago.”
**Question 5:** Is the wrist pain associated with **any injury**, insect bite, or **skin wound** near the wrist?
“Doctor, I don’t have any history of injury to the wrist, and I didn’t notice any insect bites or skin wounds near it.”
**Question 6:** Do you have any **history of blood disorders** (anemia, leukemia/low platelets), or do you bruise/bleed easily (nosebleeds, gum bleeding, heavy bruising)?
“Doctor, I’ve never been told I have any blood disorder, and I don’t bruise or bleed easily—I haven’t had nosebleeds or bleeding gums, and no unusual bruising.”
**Question 7:** Are the purple bumps/blisters **blanchable** when you press on them (turn white briefly), or do they **stay purple**?
“Doctor, when I press on the purple bumps/blisters, they don’t turn white—they stay purple.”
**Question 8:** Do you have **shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing blood**, or any **severe headache/neurologic symptoms**?
“Doctor, no—I haven’t had shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood, and I don’t have severe headaches or any numbness/weakness.”
**Question 9:** Is the wrist swelling mostly **one joint** (left wrist only), or do you have **pain/swelling in other joints** as well?

“Doctor, it’s mostly the left wrist—swelling and severe tenderness are mainly there. I haven’t had pain or swelling in any other joints besides that one episode of left knee pain last week that went away on its own.”
**Question 10:** Any **history of gout** (high uric acid, prior similar attacks), or do you eat/drink anything that might trigger it (e.g., heavy alcohol, shellfish)?

“Doctor, I’ve never been told I have gout, and I don’t know of high uric acid. I haven’t had any pattern like alcohol or shellfish triggering attacks—I just had that one left knee pain last week that resolved.”
**Question 11:** Do you have any **risk factors for endocarditis**—for example, a heart valve problem, prior endocarditis, IV drug use, or recent dental/gum infection?
“Doctor, I don’t have any known heart valve problems, I’ve never had endocarditis, and I don’t use IV drugs. I haven’t had any recent dental or gum infections that I’m aware of.”
**Question 12:** When you say the wrist hurts even with **passive movement**, do you also have **marked redness/warmth over the joint**, and is the pain out of proportion to what you see on the skin?

“Doctor, yes—the left wrist is clearly swollen, red, and feels warm, and the tenderness is much more intense than I’d expect from what I can see. The pain is really severe even when someone else moves my wrist passively.”
**Question 13:** Any **immunosuppression** (steroids, chemo, transplant), **diabetes**, or known autoimmune disease?
“Doctor, I’m otherwise healthy—no steroids, chemo, transplant, diabetes, or known autoimmune disease. I haven’t been on any immunosuppressing meds.”
**Question 14:** Have you noticed **rapid progression** of the wrist swelling over hours, or any **skin discoloration/necrosis** around the blisters (black areas), or **numbness**?

“Doctor, it seemed to worsen over a day and wasn’t over just a few minutes, and I haven’t noticed any black/necrotic skin areas or numbness—just the purple, painless blisters on both wrists and hands.”
